_meta.law: THE REGISTRY. surfaces/index.html and surfaces/doors/*.html are GENERATED from this file by tools/build-surfaces.mjs — never hand-edited. e2e/estate-source.mjs rebuilds and fails if the committed HTML has drifted, so an edit that skips this file cannot survive a gate. Add a surface here and it appears on the hub and behind its door at once.
_meta.i18n: Every generated string carries a data-i18n key so surfaces/lang.js can swap it. Keys are mechanical: a surface is s.<path-with-slashes-and-dots-as-dashes>, a domain is d.<id>.<field>. Missing translations fall back to English visibly and are counted — the corpus law, unchanged.
_meta.sorted_by: workflow wf_635765f1-ce1 — every surface opened and judged, then a challenge pass for forced fits and roadmap claims
_meta.binding_rule: A door may not claim anything the estate does not currently do. state:"roadmap" never appears among a door’s open surfaces — only under "not built yet".
_meta.slugs: A domain's FILE NAME is its slug, kept separate from its id: the published URLs (doors/beehivenature.html …) were already handed out, and a generator that renames a live URL breaks every link anyone saved. id is for CSS and data attributes; slug is for the path.
_meta.band: Each domain declares how many comb layers its header carries (founder, 2026-08-26: plur three, skaists two). A layer is a full comb at its own scale, speed, drift direction and opacity — back layers big/slow/dim, front small/quick/bright — so the eye reads depth from the layers disagreeing about how fast the world moves.
_meta.translated_strings: Any field rendered with a data-i18n key (domain who/what/intro/act, surface name/verb/caveat) is a TRANSLATED string: editing its English strands 26 tongues on the old sentence until the corpus is redrafted. e2e/estate-source.mjs now fails on that drift.
_meta.origin: A domain may carry an origin line — the founding story of its NAME, rendered above the fold on its door, ahead of everything else a stranger reads. It is a translated string like any other (d.<id>.origin), so its English cannot be edited without redrafting the corpus.

domains.label: THE ORGANISM · START HERE
domains.who: for someone who just heard the name
domains.what: A hive, not a company. One organism across five more doors — and the place the galleries live. Everything here is free to open, and nothing asks for a password, a wallet, or your name.
domains.intro: The organism's front door and the whole identity journey in one place: get started, receive, your two addresses, offline recovery — beside the wallet, the .b name desk, and the open hardware that will hold the keys. The Dock grades itself: every claim carries a receipt or is marked UNVERIFIED and stops there. The nine hosted twins of the founder's 2026-08-03 build night live here too, nine of them carrying behaviour fixes beyond the vendored chart library; the originals under surfaces/fleet/ stay byte-for-byte.

act.label: See what is proven
act.sub: The Dock grades this estate against itself — every claim carries a receipt, or is marked UNVERIFIED and stops there. Start with what we can prove.

domains.intro: Peace · love · unity · respect. The floor came before the industry did, and Wing IV of the mUseUm is the ritual the kandi bar actually enforces in code: right arm trades, left arm keeps, and the crossing moves only when something lands back.

act.label: Make a kandi and give it away
act.sub: String beads, spell a word, name who it is for — then gift it, cross it, or show it. It travels as a short line of text you carry yourself. No account, no inbox.

domains.origin: skaists is Latvian for beautiful. Karulis traces it to two roots — skaidrs, clear, and kaist, to glow — and the sense ran hot, then flushed, then bright, then beautiful. Its third dictionary sense is beautiful AND good: morally worth something, socially useful.

domains.label: THE SOCIAL LAYER · BSKY-STYLE APP IN WAITING
domains.what: The social layer: the feed, the meetings, the room. No marketplace — nothing here is for sale. Tongues dock as first-class passengers, and your name stays in your own language.
domains.intro: The social layer, ATProto-shaped. Tongues dock as first-class passengers, your name stays in your own language and aliases are pointers, never ownership. The symposium is receipted discourse; the studios and the hearth are rooms where you co-create with the hive and each other — no server anywhere.

act.label: Open the room
act.sub: Two tabs, one shared field — open it in a second tab and both hands move the same piece. No server holds it.

notYet: the pointer grammar that carries a message exists; the transport does not. Not built, said plainly.

domains.label: THE HEALTH COMMONS
domains.who: for a scientist, or anyone with a health question
domains.what: The health commons. Read food honestly — what is covered, what is not, and the denominator on every cell. Evidence is graded, and where the grade is weak the page says so instead of rounding up.
domains.intro: The health commons. The bFood hexagon replaces the pyramid because a pyramid was a ranking and food is not ranked — every cell shows n/m so you can see the denominator, and nothing is silently zero. The labs and trackers are the founder’s own instruments; where a figure is a hypothesis, the page says hypothesis.

act.label: Read the hexagon
act.sub: The successor to the food pyramid: a pyramid was a ranking, and food is not ranked. Every cell shows n/m so you can see the denominator, and nothing is ever silently zero.

domains.label: FEED THE ORGANISM
domains.who: for someone with a machine to contribute
domains.what: Feed the organism. The storage network our data lives on runs on ordinary machines, and the two treasuries that pay for it are readable by anyone, keylessly, right now.
domains.intro: “beehivebiomass.com is the civilian marketplace” — the founder’s own words. The storage network our data lives on runs on ordinary machines, and the two treasuries that pay for it read keylessly with failover: a failed read renders amber and breaks the line, because a gap is data. Running a node docks locally (antd), never through a hosted page.
